classification.difficultyReason: Normalise a two-level PDF, accumulate its areas into a continuous piecewise CDF and subtract endpoint values.

content.prompt:
A PDF is defined by
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}c,&0\le x\le5,\\2c,&5<x\le10.\end{cases}$$

answer.short: Horizontal segments at $y=c$ for $0\le x\le5$ and $y=2c$ for $5<x\le10$.
answer.worked: The density is constant at $c$ on $[0,5]$ and at $2c$ on $(5,10]$. At $x=5$, the point at height $c$ is closed and the point at height $2c$ is open.

spec.description: Two horizontal PDF segments with endpoint markers corrected to agree with the printed definition. Ordinary graph marks use black.
spec.mathematics: f(x)=c on [0,5] and f(x)=2c on (5,10]; x ticks 2,4,6,8,10; y levels c and 2c.

answer.worked:
The total area under the PDF is $1$.
$$\begin{align*}5c+5(2c)&=1\\15c&=1\\c&=\frac1{15}.\end{align*}$$

Accumulate the area from the left boundary. On the support,
$$\begin{aligned}F(x)&=\begin{cases}cx=\dfrac{x}{15},&0\le x<5,\\[4pt]5c+2c(x-5)=2cx-5c=\dfrac{2x}{15}-\dfrac13,&5\le x\le10.\end{cases}\end{aligned}$$
Thus the complete CDF is
$$F(x)=\begin{cases}0,&x<0,\\[4pt]\dfrac{x}{15},&0\le x<5,\\[4pt]\dfrac{2x}{15}-\dfrac13,&5\le x\le10,\\[4pt]1,&x>10.\end{cases}$$
